tools_problematic.problem: The installed winapp CLI has no build command, so the skill-prescribed command printed help and exited 1.

tool_limitations.limitation: Event 1000 supplied wrapper code 0xe0434352, while event 1026 contained the actionable managed HRESULT 0x8001010E. The helper discarded that HRESULT and emitted a generic managed-exception hint.
tool_limitations.suggested_tweak: Parse the event 1026 HRESULT, preserve it separately, and use it to select the startup hint.

tool_limitations.limitation: Target discovery expects a completed host-architecture packaged layout; a default non-platform build or a concurrent rebuild can produce unavailable/incomplete-layout results.
tool_limitations.suggested_tweak: Document and enforce native host-architecture build completion before launch.

failed_apis.why_tried: It is the SDK-generated WinUI application entry path.
failed_apis.root_cause: The process failed before the application initialization callback with RPC_E_WRONG_THREAD. The exact template/package compatibility cause was not resolved in the trial.
failed_apis.fix: Do not replace the generated entry point with an equivalent Program.cs. Reproduce a pristine scaffold with the same template/package set, then repair or update that matched toolchain if the scaffold also fails.

doc_errors.where: SKILL.md Step 3 and final build instruction
doc_errors.correct: Use dotnet build with the host Platform, then run Test-AppLaunch.ps1 only after the build exits successfully.

special_apis.special_handling: The copied data sources compiled after moving their XAML data namespace to Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Data; no scenario-specific rewrite was evidenced. Runtime behavior remained untestable because startup failed before a window rendered.

errors_encountered.root_cause: The scaffold types used the new project namespace while copied UWP pages retained the original sample namespace.
errors_encountered.fix: Add explicit using directives across the scaffold/source namespace boundary rather than globally renaming copied XAML classes.

errors_encountered.error: winapp build exited 1 and printed CLI help
errors_encountered.root_cause: The migration skill prescribed a command not supported by the installed CLI.
The preceding default build did not create the host-architecture layout the helper searches.
errors_encountered.fix: Build with -p:Platform=x64 on this host before launching.

errors_encountered.root_cause: The copied UWP manifest referenced sample-branded assets absent from the scaffold Assets directory; a concurrent launch also observed stale pre-rebuild output.
errors_encountered.fix: Point every manifest image reference at an existing scaffold asset and complete the rebuild before launch.

errors_encountered.root_cause: The WinUI application failed before its initialization callback; the trial did not establish whether the installed alpha template and resolved Windows App SDK package were compatible.
errors_encountered.fix: Compare against a pristine scaffold with the same versions; repair the matched toolchain rather than hand-copying the generated entry point.

errors_encountered.root_cause: The lambda parameter was named underscore, so '_ = new App()' assigned App to ApplicationInitializationCallbackParams instead of acting as a discard.
errors_encountered.fix: Use 'new App();' or rename the callback parameter.

errors_encountered.root_cause: The agent launched while the dependent rebuild was still in flight.

dev_agent_struggles.symptom: The documented build command failed, then the first launch helper call could not find x64 output.
dev_agent_struggles.turns_or_retries: Two build commands and one unavailable launch.
dev_agent_struggles.root_cause: The skill used a nonexistent winapp build command and did not state the helper's host-architecture build contract prominently.
dev_agent_struggles.how_resolved: The agent switched to dotnet build and then added -p:Platform=x64.
dev_agent_struggles.preventable_by: A correct, copyable dotnet build -p:Platform=<host-arch> command immediately before the launch helper.

dev_agent_struggles.symptom: Repeated startup launches, event-log inspection, a speculative custom Program.cs, another compile error, and packaged/unpackaged retries did not resolve the crash.
dev_agent_struggles.turns_or_retries: At least four crash/unavailable launch attempts after manifest repair.
dev_agent_struggles.root_cause: The helper hid managed HRESULT 0x8001010E behind native wrapper code 0xe0434352, and the startup guidance did not distinguish SDK-generated Program.Main from authored code.
dev_agent_struggles.how_resolved: Unresolved; the agent correctly reported the migration incomplete.
dev_agent_struggles.preventable_by: Managed-HRESULT-aware diagnostics plus a generated-entry-point decision rule that requires a pristine scaffold comparison before app-code edits.

missing_tooling.need: A pristine scaffold compatibility preflight or explicit scaffold comparison workflow.
missing_tooling.would_have_saved: It would have separated template/package startup failure from migrated application code before the agent spent multiple turns rewriting Program.cs.

env_issues.issue: dotnet new reported Microsoft.WindowsAppSDK.WinUI.CSharp.Templates 0.0.5-alpha with 0.0.6-alpha available, while post-actions resolved Microsoft.WindowsAppSDK 2.3.1.
env_issues.workaround: Treat template and Windows App SDK versions as a matched toolchain and verify a pristine scaffold before migration-specific diagnosis.
